GRID India Opens Applications for 15 Paid Power‑System Internships (Oct‑Nov 2026)

Overview

Grid Controller of India Limited (GRID‑India), a Miniratna‑I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Power, has issued a recruitment notification for 15 full‑time internships focused on Power System Simulation Studies. The programme, branded विद्युत प्रज्ञा, runs for six months (extendable by three months) and offers a stipend of ₹50,000 per month. Applications are accepted online from 22 October 2026 until 6 November 2026.

Eligibility criteria

  • Nationality: Indian citizens only.
  • Educational qualifications:
  • Minimum: Full‑time regular B.E./B.Tech./B.Sc. (Engg.)/Integrated Dual Degree in Electrical, Electrical‑Power, Electrical & Electronics, Power Systems Engineering or Power Engineering (Electrical) with ≥ 65 % or equivalent CGPA.
  • Candidates with a M.Tech./M.E./MSR in Power Systems or a related field are also eligible, as are Ph.D. scholars in the same area, provided they obtain a No‑Objection Certificate from their institution.
  • Age: 18 – 32 years as of 6 Nov 2026 (relaxations follow Government of India directives).
  • Academic status: The undergraduate degree must be completed on or before the closing date. Applicants awaiting final results or pending degree completion are ineligible.
  • Prior employment: Preference is given to candidates who have not been previously employed. Applicants must not have availed benefits under the PM Internship Scheme or any central/state apprenticeship scheme.

Application process and timeline

  • Online portal – Applications must be submitted through the official GRID‑India website (link provided below). No paper applications are accepted.
  • Form completion – Applicants must enter personal, academic and contact details, and verify that CGPA calculations are correct where applicable.
  • Submission deadline – All entries must be uploaded on or before 6 Nov 2026. Late submissions will be rejected.
  • Shortlisting – The selection committee will first shortlist candidates who meet the essential criteria. Preference will be given to those with desirable qualifications (e.g., higher degrees, relevant projects).
  • Interaction at NLDC – Shortlisted candidates are invited for an on‑site interaction at the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC), New Delhi. No travel or DA allowance is provided for this stage.

Stipend, duration and working conditions

  • Stipend: ₹50,000 per month, all‑inclusive. No additional allowances, benefits or emoluments are payable.
  • Duration: Six months, with a possible three‑month extension on mutual agreement, under the same terms.
  • Location: Interns will be posted at the NLDC in New Delhi or one of the five Regional Load Despatch Centres (RLDCs). Candidates may indicate a preferred location; placement will depend on vacancy availability.
  • On‑site requirement: Interns must be present full‑time at the assigned centre for the entire internship period. Travel and accommodation costs are the intern’s responsibility.
  • Taxation: Stipend recipients are liable for any applicable taxes.

Training focus

Interns will work in Power System Simulation Studies, gaining hands‑on experience with simulation and modelling tools used in the Indian power grid. The programme aims to build expertise needed for renewable‑energy integration and emerging grid technologies.

Practical implications for aspirants

  • Career entry point: While the internship does not guarantee subsequent employment with GRID‑India, the exposure to national load‑dispatch operations can strengthen a candidate’s profile for future power‑sector roles.
  • Financial considerations: The stipend is competitive for internships in the public sector, but candidates must budget for personal travel, lodging and daily expenses.
  • Academic timing: Final‑year undergraduates must ensure their degree is awarded before the deadline; otherwise they are disqualified.
  • Location flexibility: Preference can be expressed, but candidates should be prepared for placement at any of the six centres.
